diagnostics.message: module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:output.access_key_id: explicit depends_on of module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:resource.aws_iam_access_key.this_user is redundant — already implied by attribute references
module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:output.access_secret_key: explicit depends_on of module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:resource.aws_iam_access_key.this_user is redundant — already implied by attribute references

Output module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:output.access_key_id has an explicit depends_on on aws_iam_access_key.this_user, but its value already reads aws_iam_access_key.this_user.id, which establishes the same dependency implicitly. The depends_on is redundant.

Output module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:output.access_secret_key has an explicit depends_on on aws_iam_access_key.this_user, but its value already reads aws_iam_access_key.this_user.secret (same resource), which establishes the dependency implicitly. The depends_on is redundant.

helm_release.elk installs the ELK chart whose elasticsearch pods reference kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_credentials by secretKeyRef name only; nothing creates a Terraform ordering edge. The release (helm --wait) can start before the secret exists, leaving pods in CreateContainerConfigError.

helm_release.elk mounts the "elastic-certificates" secret (secretMounts) created by kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates, but only by literal name, so no implicit dependency exists. The release can be applied before the TLS secret is created.

helm_release.elk's elasticsearch keystore references kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_s3_user_creds by name only (keystore.secretName). No attribute reference or depends_on orders the release after the S3 credentials secret.
helm_release.elk's kibana pods read the "kibana-encryption-key" secret via secretKeyRef, created by kubernetes_secret.kibana_enc_key, but the reference is only a literal name with no dependency edge.

helm_release.elk provisions an Elasticsearch PVC with storageClassName "advanced", but nothing references kubernetes_storage_class.advanced. On a fresh apply the release can be created before the StorageClass exists, leaving the PVC unbound and the helm --wait install timing out.

helm_release.prometheus_operator creates a Prometheus PVC with storageClassName "advanced" but has no dependency on kubernetes_storage_class.advanced; the release can race ahead of the StorageClass existing.

helm_release.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack creates a vmsingle PVC with storageClassName "advanced" but does not depend on kubernetes_storage_class.advanced, so it may be applied before the StorageClass exists.

helm_release.loki_stack provisions Loki persistence with storageClassName "advanced" but has no dependency on kubernetes_storage_class.advanced, so the release can be created before the StorageClass exists.
